content:
release-manager: Heads up — deploy-bot is failing to push the 2026.03.20 release images to us-east-1 ECR during the release window. Logs show repeated 429s and a manifest upload error. Can we triage?

deploy-bot: [system] push failed: PutImageManifest -> 429 TooManyRequests. last_error_id=pb-98f3

alex: saw the 429 spike earlier, looks like backend started throttling on multipart uploads. Are these large multi-arch manifests or lots of parallel CI pushes?

jordan: single build tried to push 4 arch manifests + SBOM attestation in parallel. CI retried twice, then deploy-bot attempted the staged publish.

sre-oncall: yep that matches a short-lived quota saturation on the registry side. We can either backoff/retry with exponential jitter or divert the publish to another region/replica. Which is less risky for this rollout?

maria: product wants the release to go out in this window for the promo. If we divert region, will latency or compliance be impacted?

seb: divert to eu-west will be fine for non-EU customers, but the release pipeline expects us-east image digests (tags are sync'd by CI). If we republish in eu we still need to sync digests and update the deploybot routing. extra coordination overhead.

alex: short checklist: 1) avoid double-pushing the same digest 2) avoid creating ephemeral tags that confuse canaries 3) if we can't publish new digest, pin to previous stable digest for canary/rollout.

release-manager: proposal: hold the global rollout, run a canary pointing at the stable digest from last successful build (digest: sha256:7af3b2...), and meanwhile try a manual republish with reduced concurrency and longer backoff. Thoughts?

jordan: I can trigger a manual republish from the build artifact: build-id=2026-03-20-58. Commands I'll run (dry run first):

```
# login and fetch manifest
aws ecr get-login-password --region us-east-1 | docker login --username AWS --password-stdin 123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com
aws ecr batch-get-image --repository-name my-app --image-ids imageTag=2026-03-20-58 --region us-east-1 --output json > manifest.json
# push with single-threaded put-image calls
aws ecr put-image --repository-name my-app --image-tag=2026-03-20-58 --image-manifest file://manifest.json --region us-east-1
```

deploy-bot: [system] on hold per @release-manager. Canary pinned to sha256:7af3b2... on service/my-app-canary. Automatic global rollout paused.

maria: please add a short note in the release notes: "Publishing delayed due to registry backpressure; canary running on previous stable image. We expect final publish within 2 hours or will opt for a rollback."

seb: also adding a temporary fallback rule: if put-image returns >=3 consecutive 429s, pause CI pushes for 15m and notify #eng-infra. Implemented as a short patch in publish-runner.

alex: minor ops ask — let's avoid retagging the old digest to the new semver tag. Instead use an explicit deploybot pin config so tags remain immutable and audit trails stay clean.

release-manager: agreed. @deploy-bot, apply pin config for canary and record a note in the release ticket.

deploy-bot: [system] pinned service/my-app-canary -> sha256:7af3b2... (applied by release-manager). audit_id=pin-20260320-1

jordan: manual republish attempt results: two staged put-image calls succeeded after slowing concurrency; final manifest push returned 200. Will verify attestation upload next.

deploy-bot: [system] attestation upload failed: 413 PayloadTooLarge when posting SBOM to signing endpoint. Falling back to deferred attestation.

seb: deferred attestation is okay short-term, but we need to make sure policies accept deferred flags for the release. I'll file a quick exception with the compliance bot and add a note to the ticket.

maria: if attestation is deferred, we should be explicit in the release notes that final release will include attestation and any delayed audits. PMs notified. :white_check_mark:

release-manager: decision: keep canary pinned to stable digest for now; accept manual republish to us-east for the new digest but delay global rollout until attestation completes or compliance signs off. Update release notes and hold the change window.

alex: +1. I'll follow up with a small change to publish-runner to reduce parallelism by default for big manifests.

jordan: tagging note: created a tandem tag `2026.03.20-pending-attest` on the new digest (no overwrite of latest). Command used: `aws ecr put-image --repository-name my-app --image-tag=2026.03.20-pending-attest --image-manifest file://manifest.json`

deploy-bot: [system] release window paused; global rollout blocked. last_action=pin-canary, pending=attestation, contact=@seb for infra.

release-manager: thanks everyone. I'll update the release ticket + slack channel with the hold reason and ETA. If attestation lands earlier we can resume within the same window; otherwise we'll reschedule the full rollout. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
